title: Fluctuation-based evidence for number--phase dynamics in a frustrated orbital superfluid
authors: Rui-Lang Zeng, Zi-Yao Zhang, Ling-Na Wu, Cong-Jie Zhang, Da-Gang Xia, Andreas Hemmerich, Xiao-Qiong Wang, Zhi-Fang Xu
abstract: Frustrated quantum matter can host intertwined orders rooted in symmetry-related low-energy landscapes, yet static order parameters alone do not reveal how fluctuations are organized among competing configurations. Here we measure mode-resolved shot-to-shot population fluctuations in a $p$-orbital triangular-lattice superfluid with a tunable bias among three valleys. We observe a bias-tuned evolution from enhanced, anticorrelated fluctuations of two minority valleys toward strong confinement of relative-population fluctuations in a selected two-valley stripe phase. The dominant fluctuation structure is captured by an effective canonical model that includes interactions among the condensed modes, supporting a quasi-equilibrium description of the coherent three-valley condensate. Together, the data and model reveal a quantum--thermal regime shaped by pair-tunneling-induced number--phase dynamics, in which relative-phase scrambling softens effective barriers in the minority-valley regime, while phase rigidity gives rise to macroscopic harmonic confinement in the stripe phase. Our results establish mode-resolved fluctuation measurements as a probe of hidden number--phase back-action in frustrated quantum fluids.
summary: The paper investigates number-phase dynamics in a frustrated orbital superfluid realized with ultracold atoms. By measuring mode-resolved population fluctuations, the authors distinguish between two distinct physical mechanisms: barrier softening due to quantum thermal effects in one regime, and phase rigidity leading to harmonic confinement in another. This establishes fluctuation measurements as a powerful diagnostic tool for understanding complex interacting quantum fluids.
main_problem: The study aims to reveal how fluctuations are organized among competing orders in frustrated quantum matter, as static order parameters fail to capture the full dynamics.
main_result: The research demonstrates that number-phase dynamics manifest differently depending on bias: phase scrambling softens barriers in minority-valley regimes, while phase rigidity induces harmonic confinement in stripe phases.
method: The authors measure mode-resolved shot-to-shot population fluctuations and compare these experimental data against effective canonical models derived from a three-mode Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is an ultracold gas of atoms loaded into the $p$-orbital band of a 2D triangular optical lattice, realizing a minimal three-valley superfluid. The dynamics are governed by an effective three-mode Hamiltonian including bias and pair-tunneling terms.
key_observables: Mode-resolved shot-to-shot population fluctuations ($\Delta n_i$), correlation coefficients ($C_{23}$), normalized relative variance ($\sigma^2_{	ext{rel}}$), and the total collective susceptibility $(\Delta n)^2$.
important_parameters: Tunable valley bias ($\Delta E$), temperature/density ratio ($T/N$), and comparison between quantum zero-point motion and thermal limits.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the dynamics onto an effective canonical model, using harmonic expansions around phase-locked minima in certain regimes, and acknowledging limitations due to finite-time relaxation or spatial averaging.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $\Delta n_i$ vs. bias showing non-monotonic behavior; $C_{23}$ shows dips indicating binary competition; $(\Delta n)^2$ peaks at degeneracy; and the final figure compares measured relative variance ($\sigma^2_{	ext{rel}}$) to harmonic oscillator fits in the stripe phase.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes fluctuation signatures across different bias regimes: first, showing how fluctuations reveal hidden number-phase back-action; second, quantifying correlations ($C_{23}$) and susceptibility $(\Delta n)^2$; finally, contrasting barrier softening (negative bias) with phase rigidity/harmonic confinement (positive bias).
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed experimental roadmap for using fluctuation measurements to probe complex quantum many-body physics in ultracold atomic systems, linking measurable noise statistics directly to underlying Hamiltonian symmetries and dynamics.
